newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba hails world support against U.S. embargo.
newsitem.headline: Cuba hails world support against U.S. embargo.

text.p: Cuba on Tuesday welcomed as a "complete success" a larger-than-ever vote by the U.N. General Assembly against the longstanding U.S. economic embargo on the island.

Vice President Carlos Lage told the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina that the vote in favour of a resolution calling for an end to the embargo showed Washington's international isolation, and worldwide rejection of a U.S. move in March to toughen the sanctions.
"It is a complete success and a victory for the revolution and for our people," said Lage, who spoke for Cuba at Tuesday's General Assembly session on the embargo.

It was the fifth consecutive year that the General Assembly has adopted a resolution calling for an end to the embargo, which is more than three decades old. The vote this year, a larger majority than ever, was 137 to three, with 25 abstentions. This compared with 117 to three, with 38 abstentions in a similar vote last year.
Lage noted that the number of abstentions had dropped.

For example, all 15 members of the European Union voted in favour of the resolution, whereas last year Britain, Germany and the Netherlands had abstained. In Latin America and the Caribbean, only Guatemala and El Salvadar abstained while the rest of the region voted with the resolution.

International criticism of U.S. policy has sharpened because of the Helms-Burton law, adopted by the U.S. Congress earlier this year. It allows U.S. citizens who were Cuban nationals before the 1959 communist revolution to sue in U.S. courts foreign companies or individuals who "traffic" in property confiscated by the government of President Fidel Castro.
